text:
ara: Heads-up: we rolled 0.10.0 to staging and saw socket exhaustion under concurrent tests. Reverted to 0.9.2 and failure went away.

tom: thanks for the signal. short description of trigger?

ara: pattern that breaks: creating RedwoodAsyncClient inside request handler / dependency (so many short-lived clients). 0.10.0 changed connector defaults -> unlimited connections when connector.limit=0. Previously limit=100.

nina: oh nice catch. did 0.10 touch adapter/connector code?

ara: PR #312 introduced the new http adapter and defaulted to no explicit limit. Works fine for single shared client but awful if people create per-request.

tom: immediate mitigation: update our sample apps and quickstart to explicitly show lifespan/shared-client pattern + add lint warnings in examples. Also rollback prod if customers are impacted.

nina: SDK fixes I propose: 
- set safe default connector limit=100
- runtime warning when client is garbage-collected without calling .close() or async __aexit__
- add contextmanager examples for FastAPI/Starlette and gunicorn+uvicorn notes (workers vs processes)
- small helper factory `make_shared_client()` for web frameworks

ara: also found small typing bug: AsyncClient.__aenter__/__aexit__ missing from stub, so editors don't autocomplete context usage. Could add typing tests.

tom: add a CI e2e concurrency test to catch regressions that spin up many short-lived clients. Make it opt-in for PRs that touch http layer (fast).

ci-bot: ticket SDK-478 created for default pool fix + runtime warning. CI job scheduled.

nina: plan for release: 0.10.1 patch with bounded default + docs + example updates. Mark as critical.

ara: I'll push the repro harness and a minimal load script to ci/artifacts/1725067890 so reviewers can run locally.

tom: great. let's also add a short FAQ entry: "Why am I seeing many TIME_WAIT sockets?" with clear code snippets.

nina: filed PR #355 (connpool-defaults + typing stubs + examples).

ara: thanks team. lesson: defaulting to "more permissive" for perf can be a DX regression. :sweat_smile:
